name: Accounting
summary: Learn to record, report, audit and analyse the money side of organisations, and prepare for professional exams like ICAN, ACCA or CPA.
overview:
Accounting is the language of business. Accountants record what an organisation earns, owns and owes, turn that into financial statements people can trust, and use the numbers to help managers decide what to do next.

The degree starts with the principles of double-entry bookkeeping, economics and business maths. It then builds through financial and cost accounting to the core professional subjects: financial reporting under IFRS, auditing, taxation, management accounting and corporate finance. Most programmes include an industrial placement and a final-year research project.

An accounting degree pairs naturally with a professional qualification (ICAN or ANAN in Nigeria, ACCA or ICAEW in the UK, CPA in the US), and many universities give exemptions from some of those papers.
durationNotes: 4 years in Nigeria and the US; usually 3 years in England, or 4 with a placement year.

subjects: Two of: Financial Accounting, Commerce, Government, Geography, or another subject
entryRequirements.notes: Five credits in not more than two sittings. Check your chosen university's exact subject list.

subjects: One other Arts or Social Science subject (e.g. Principles of Accounts, Commerce, Government)
Mathematics, Economics or Accounting are helpful
entryRequirements.notes: Most universities also ask for a good GCSE pass in Mathematics.

careers.title: Chartered accountant
careers.description: Prepares and advises on financial statements, often in a firm, after passing professional exams.

careers.title: Auditor
careers.description: Independently checks that an organisation's financial statements are true and fair.

careers.title: Tax consultant
careers.description: Helps individuals and companies comply with tax law and plan their tax position.

careers.title: Management accountant or financial analyst
careers.description: Works inside a business on budgets, costs, forecasts and investment decisions.

careers.title: Forensic accountant
careers.description: Investigates fraud and financial disputes, sometimes as an expert witness.

careers.title: Public sector accountant
careers.description: Manages and reports public funds in government ministries, agencies and NGOs.

stages.title: Year 1
stages.summary: Double-entry bookkeeping, economics and the maths of business.

stages.title: Year 2
stages.summary: Company accounts, costing, business law and accounting systems.

stages.title: Year 3
stages.summary: The core professional subjects (IFRS, audit, tax, management accounting and finance) plus industrial training.

stages.title: Final year
stages.summary: Group accounts, advanced audit, public sector accounting, electives and a research project.

nodes.title: Principles of Accounting
nodes.description: The foundation of everything that follows: the accounting equation, double-entry bookkeeping, books of original entry, the trial balance and simple final accounts.

resources.title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting (OpenStax)

nodes.title: Principles of Economics
nodes.description: Microeconomics (how households and firms make choices, supply and demand, market structures) and macroeconomics (inflation, unemployment, interest rates and government policy).

nodes.title: Business Mathematics and Statistics
nodes.description: The quantitative tools accountants use daily: percentages, interest and discounting, basic algebra, and descriptive statistics and probability.

nodes.title: Introduction to Business and Management
nodes.description: How organisations are structured and run: forms of business, management functions, marketing, operations and the business environment.

nodes.title: Spreadsheets for accountants
nodes.description: Excel or Google Sheets skills that save hours: formulas, lookups, pivot tables and clean layout. Employers expect them from day one.

nodes.title: Financial Accounting
nodes.description: Preparing full financial statements for sole traders, partnerships and companies, including adjustments, depreciation, inventory valuation and cash flow statements.
keyConcepts: Company accounts and cash flow statements

nodes.title: Cost Accounting
nodes.description: Working out what products and services really cost: material, labour and overhead costing, job and process costing, and marginal versus absorption costing.

resources.title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting (OpenStax)

nodes.title: Business and Company Law
nodes.description: The legal rules businesses operate under: contracts, agency, partnership, and company law such as Nigeria's Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020.

nodes.title: Accounting Information Systems
nodes.description: How accounting data is captured, processed and controlled in software, from ledgers and ERP systems to internal controls over them.

resources.title: GnuCash: free accounting software to practise on

nodes.title: Financial Reporting (IFRS)
nodes.description: Preparing financial statements under International Financial Reporting Standards, which Nigeria, the UK and over 140 other jurisdictions require for listed companies.

nodes.title: Auditing and Assurance
nodes.description: How auditors gather evidence to give an opinion on financial statements: planning, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and reporting.

nodes.title: Taxation
nodes.description: How individuals and companies are taxed: personal income tax, company income tax, VAT and capital gains, plus tax administration. Tax law changes often (Nigeria overhauled its tax laws in 2025), so always check the current rules.

nodes.title: Management Accounting
nodes.description: Using accounting information to plan and control a business: budgeting, standard costing and variances, decision-making and performance measurement.

resources.title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting (OpenStax)

nodes.title: Corporate Finance
nodes.description: How companies decide what to invest in and how to pay for it: time value of money, investment appraisal, cost of capital, and working capital management.

resources.title: Corporate finance lectures and notes (Aswath Damodaran, NYU)

nodes.title: Industrial training (SIWES or placement)
nodes.description: Work in an accounting firm, a company's finance team or a public body. In Nigeria this is the SIWES placement; in the UK it's an optional placement year. Audit firms often hire from their interns.

nodes.title: Advanced Financial Reporting
nodes.description: Reporting for groups of companies and complex transactions: consolidation, associates and joint ventures, financial instruments, and interpreting financial statements.

resources.title: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements summary (IAS Plus)

nodes.title: Advanced Audit and Assurance
nodes.description: Audit of groups and complex entities, assurance engagements beyond the financial statements, quality management, and current issues like data analytics in audit.

nodes.title: Public Sector Accounting
nodes.description: How governments and public bodies budget, account for and report public money, including International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS).
keyConcepts: Accountability and audit of public funds

nodes.title: Professional Ethics and Governance
nodes.description: The ethical code accountants must follow (integrity, objectivity, competence, confidentiality and professional behaviour) and how corporate governance protects investors.

resources.title: International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (IESBA)

nodes.title: Research Project
nodes.description: An independent study of an accounting or finance question, such as the effect of IFRS adoption or tax reform, written up as a dissertation.

nodes.title: Forensic Accounting and Fraud Examination
nodes.description: How financial fraud is committed, detected and investigated, and how forensic accountants present evidence.

resources.title: Fraud resources (Association of Certified Fraud Examiners)

nodes.title: Data Analytics for Accountants
nodes.description: Analyse financial data at scale with Power BI and SQL: cleaning data, building dashboards and spotting anomalies. Increasingly expected in audit and finance roles.

nodes.title: Sustainability Reporting
nodes.description: Reporting on climate and other sustainability risks under the ISSB's IFRS S1 and S2 standards, which more countries (including Nigeria) are adopting.

nodes.title: Professional qualifications
nodes.description: Plan your route to chartered status: ICAN or ANAN in Nigeria, ACCA or ICAEW internationally, or CPA in the US. Check which papers your degree exempts you from.

resources.title: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN)
